readings.subsection: The Uncontained Essence of the Creator
readings.title: Righteousness and the Mortal Realm
readings.subtitle: Human Actions Cannot Diminish the Almighty
readings.text: [Job 35:1] And Elihu responded and said, [2] “Do you think this is right? Do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than that of <dn>Ēl</dn>’? [3] For you say, ‘Of what use is it to you? What do I gain more than if I had sinned?’ [4] Let me answer you and <dn>את</dn> your friends with you. [5] Look to the heavens, and see. And consider the clouds which are higher than you. [6] If you sin, what would you do against <dn>Him</dn>? If your transgressions are increased, what would you do to <dn>Him</dn>? [7] If you are righteous, what do you give <dn>Him</dn>? Or what does <dn>He</dn> receive from your hand? [8] Your wrong is for a man like yourself, and your righteousness for a son of man.

readings.title: The Rejection of Prideful Petitions
readings.subtitle: Waiting for the Right-Ruling of Eloah
readings.text: [9] Because of the multitude of oppressions they cry out; they cry out for help because of the arm of the many. [10] And no one says, ‘Where is <dn>Eloah</dn> my Maker, who gives songs in the night, [11] teaching us more than the beasts of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the heavens?’ [12] There they cry, but <dn>He</dn> answers not, because of the pride of evil ones. [13] Only, it is false that <dn>Ēl</dn> does not hear, and that the <dn>Almighty</dn> pays no attention to it. [14] Although you say you do not see <dn>Him</dn>, yet right-ruling is before <dn>Him</dn>, and you wait for <dn>Him</dn>. [15] And now, is it for naught that <dn>His</dn> displeasure has come? Yet <dn>He</dn> has not taken note of extreme arrogance, [16] so Iyoḇ opens his mouth in vain, he increases words without knowledge.”

readings.title: Discipline as the Hedge of Protection
readings.subtitle: Restoration Through Repentance and Obedience
readings.text: [Job 36:1] Then Elihu continued and said, [2] “Bear with me a little, and let me show you there is still more to say for <dn>Eloah</dn>. [3] I bring my knowledge from afar and ascribe righteousness to my Maker. [4] For truly my words are not false; the <dn>One</dn> perfect in knowledge is with you. [5] See, <dn>Ēl</dn> is mighty, but rejects no one – mighty in power and heart. [6] <dn>He</dn> does not keep the wrongdoer alive, but <dn>He</dn> gives right-ruling to the oppressed ones. [7] <dn>He</dn> does not withdraw <dn>His</dn> eyes from the righteous, and <dn>את</dn> sovereigns on the throne, and seats them forever, and they are exalted. [8] And if they are bound in shackles, caught in the cords of affliction, [9] then <dn>He</dn> reveals to them their work, and their transgressions, that they behaved proudly. [10] And <dn>He</dn> opens their ear for discipline, and commands that they turn back from wickedness. [11] If they obey and serve, they complete their days in blessedness, and their years in pleasantness. [12] But if they do not obey, they perish by the sword, and die without knowledge. [13] But the defiled ones in heart become enraged – let them not cry for help when <dn>He</dn> binds them. [14] Their being dies in youth, and their life among the male cult prostitutes. [15] <dn>He</dn> rescues the afflicted one in his affliction, and opens their ears in oppression.

readings.title: The Danger of Scoffing in Judgment
readings.subtitle: Choosing Trust Over the Temptation of Wickedness
readings.text: [16] And <dn>He</dn> also would have brought you out of distress, into a broad place where there is no restraint. And what is set on your table would be filled with rich food. [17] But you are filled with the judgment of the wrong, judgment and right-ruling take hold of you. [18] Beware, that rage does not entice you to scoffing. And do not let a large bribe turn you aside. [19] Would <dn>He</dn> value your riches? No, not precious ore, nor all your strength! [20] Do not long for the night, when people go up in their place. [21] Beware, do not turn to wickedness, for you have chosen this rather than affliction.

readings.title: The Unsearchable Mechanics of Creation
readings.subtitle: The Orchestration of Rain and Lightning
readings.text: [Job 36:22] See, <dn>Ēl</dn> is exalted by <dn>His</dn> power; who is a Teacher like <dn>Him</dn>? [23] Who has appointed <dn>Him</dn> <dn>His</dn> way, or who has said, ‘You have worked unrighteousness’? [24] Remember to extol <dn>His</dn> work, of which men have sung. [25] All men have seen it, man looks on it from afar. [26] See, <dn>Ēl</dn> is great, beyond our understanding, and we do not know the number of <dn>His</dn> years. [27] For <dn>He</dn> draws up drops of water, which distil as rain from the mist, [28] which the clouds drop down – pour down in showers on man. [29] Also, who understands the spreading of clouds, the crashing from <dn>His</dn> booth? [30] See, <dn>He</dn> has spread <dn>his</dn> light upon it, and <dn>He</dn> has covered the depths of the sea. [31] For by these <dn>He</dn> judges the peoples; <dn>He</dn> gives plenty of food. [32] <dn>He</dn> has covered <dn>His</dn> hands with lightning, and commands it to strike. [33] Its noise declares concerning <dn>Him</dn>, also the cattle, as to what is coming up.

readings.subsection: The Active Physics of the Earth
readings.title: The Voice that Commands the Storm
readings.subtitle: Weather as an Instrument of Divine Right-Ruling
readings.text: [Job 37:1] “At this too my heart trembles, and leaps from its place. [2] Listen, listen to the trembling of <dn>His</dn> voice, and the sound that comes from <dn>His</dn> mouth. [3] <dn>He</dn> lets it loose under all the heavens, and <dn>His</dn> lightning to the ends of the earth. [4] After it a voice roars. <dn>He</dn> thunders with the voice of <dn>His</dn> excellency, and <dn>He</dn> does not hold them back when <dn>His</dn> voice is heard. [5] <dn>Ēl</dn> thunders wondrously with <dn>His</dn> voice; doing great deeds, which we do not understand. [6] For <dn>He</dn> says to the snow, <dq>‘Be on the earth,’</dq> also to the gentle rain and the heavy rain of <dn>His</dn> strength. [7] <dn>He</dn> seals up the hand of every man, for all men to know <dn>His</dn> work. [8] Then the beast goes into its lair, and they stay in their dens. [9] From the room of the south comes the whirlwind, and cold from the scattering winds of the north. [10] By the breath of <dn>Ēl</dn> ice is given, and the expanse of water becomes solid. [11] <dn>He</dn> also loads the thick clouds with moisture; <dn>He</dn> scatters <dn>His</dn> bright clouds. [12] And they swirl about, being turned by <dn>His</dn> guidance, to do whatever <dn>He</dn> commands them on the face of the earthly world. [13] <dn>He</dn> causes it to come, whether as a rod, or for <dn>His</dn> land, or for loving-commitment.

readings.title: Considering the Wonders of El
readings.subtitle: Reverence for the Incomprehensible Creator
readings.text: [14] Listen to this, O Iyoḇ, stand still and consider the wonders of <dn>Ēl</dn>. [15] Do you know when <dn>Eloah</dn> placed them, and caused the lightning of <dn>His</dn> cloud to shine? [16] Do you know the balancing of the clouds, the wonders of the <dn>One</dn> perfect in knowledge? [17] Why are your garments hot, when the earth is stilled from the south? [18] Did you, with <dn>Him</dn>, spread out the clouds, strong as a hard mirror? [19] Teach us what we should say to <dn>Him</dn>; we do not set in order because of darkness. [20] Should <dn>He</dn> be told that I would speak? Would any man ask to be swallowed up? [21] And now, they shall not look on the light that is bright behind the clouds, when the wind has passed and cleared them. [22] From the golden north it comes – with <dn>Eloah</dn> is awesome excellency. [23] The <dn>Almighty</dn>, we have not found <dn>Him</dn> out, <dn>He</dn> is exalted in power and right-ruling and great in righteousness – <dn>He</dn> does not oppress. [24] Therefore men fear <dn>Him</dn>. <dn>He</dn> does not regard any who are wise of heart.”
